questions.q: What did the Beginner project at Hartwell Regional Utilities accomplish?
options: Mara hardened a handful of servers and shipped one Sentinel analytics rule, for IT Manager Dale Granger
questions.explain: The Beginner project was narrower: a handful of hardened servers and one working Sentinel rule, for Dale Granger.

questions.q: What does IT Director Owen Mercer actually want from this project?
options: Real operational visibility across Windows, Linux, and the perimeter firewall
Fewer employees on the SOC team
questions.explain: Owen wants to actually see what's happening across Hartwell's environment, not just one narrow slice of it.

questions.q: What does Compliance Officer Renee Castellano actually want?
options: An auditable compliance trail: documented logging, access review, and incident-response capability
questions.explain: Renee needs evidence the controls exist and work -- documentation an auditor or regulator could review, not just a verbal assurance.

questions.q: Why does this become one project instead of two separate ones?
options: Owen and Renee coordinated in advance and wrote a joint request
Owen's and Renee's independent asks overlap: real multi-source visibility, built with real documentation and runbooks, satisfies both
Hartwell's budget only allows one project per year
Dale Granger merged the two requests himself
questions.explain: They asked independently, but a well-scoped SOC buildout with documentation satisfies both the operational-visibility ask and the compliance-trail ask.

questions.q: What regulatory framework is mentioned as a realistic driver of Renee's compliance ask?
options: NERC CIP, a set of mandatory cybersecurity standards for electric utilities
questions.explain: NERC CIP is the real, common regulatory framework electric utilities like Hartwell answer to for cybersecurity controls.
